Article Title: Rebel TMC group leader Sudip urges PM Modi to appoint NDA convener
Article Text:
Rebel Trinamool Congress leader in Lok Sabha Sudip Bandyopadhyay

NEW DELHI: Breakaway Trinamool Congress leader in Lok Sabha Sudip Bandyopadhyay has urged PM Narendra Modi to appoint a NDA convener, saying it will allow the governing alliance parties to convey their views to him and exchange ideas, more so when Parliament is not in session.He made the suggestion to Modi as he met him at the tea hosted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla for leaders of different parties on Thursday."I made the request as there is no connection and communication, especially when session is over," he said, adding that a convener will serve as a point of contact for other parties and keep the communication line open.With Birla also present, the sixth-term Lok Sabha MP urged him for an early decision on the merger of his faction 20 MPs with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).While they are now part of NDA and its second biggest constituent after BJP, they are shown as AITC (All India Trinamool Congress) MPs by Sansad TV when they speak in Lok Sabha. "Our issue should be sorted out soon," he said, adding that it allows TMC, which is now left with only eight MPs in the House, to question their group's legitimacy.While BJP allies like George Fernandes and Sharad Yadav served as NDA convener in the past, especially during the Vajpayee govt, no one has held the position for several years.TMC is, however, preparing to move the Supreme Court against the rebel Lok Sabha MPs to seek their disqualification.Party general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had met Birla on Jul 27, urging him to expedite his decision on its petition seeking disqualification of the 20 MPs.Banerjee, a Lok Sabha MP, had also sought revocation of changes made to the seating arrangements of his party’s MPs to allow the rebel members to sit separately. He had submitted separate letters to the speaker on each of his concerns.He had met the Speaker on Wednesday over the issue."If the Speaker does not decide on these petitions within the period required by law and applicable judicial directions, I will be compelled to approach the Supreme Court and seek its intervention,” Abhishek said.
Article Summary: Breakaway Trinamool Congress leader in Lok Sabha Sudip Bandyopadhyay has urged PM Narendra Modi to appoint a NDA convener. He made the suggestion to Modi as he met him at the tea hosted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.

Article Title: Gen Z led student protest taught MPs how to use humour in serious political communication: Derek O' Brien
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Hailing opposition unity evident in the way the INDIA bloc parties cornered the BJP led NDA in the monsoon session of Parliament, TMC’s Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’ Brien said that while the session that ended on Thursday belonged to the opposition, it was the protests over the NEET paper leaks at Jantar Mantar by youth that set the pitch for what followed in Parliament.“This was a session that belonged to the opposition. This was a win for the students and youth of the country. What they did till July 20, we the MPs had to just carry that forward. It was their win,” O’Brien said.“They taught us MPs how to use humour in serious political communication. What happened was because of the youth-student movement. Just from criticising the govt it went to ridiculing the govt,” he added citing examples of slogans coined by Gen Z to attack the govt during the protests. The TMC leader further said that a key takeaway from this session was that the opposition worked in a coordinated way.On Thursday all opposition parties had a casual meeting in the lobby of Rajya Sabha just to tell each other that all had worked as a team, an opposition MP said. He added that it was basically an assessment that the opposition really did well in the way it went about raising issues and there was a lot of unity.Opposition members highlighted that not just the INDIA bloc members but the opposition also found the way to create room for AAP which is no longer part of the grouping to speak and also DMK to make their point amid the protests in the House. The DMK distanced itself from the wider opposition INDIA bloc following friction with Congress since the latter severed its longstanding alliance with it and decided to support the TVK govt in Tamil Nadu.Going forward, the INDIA bloc parties have decided to keep up the momentum and build on the unity seen in the current session to counter the ruling dispensation till the winter session. There was also consensus that if the INDIA bloc is meeting anytime soon then the date should be announced in August itself. The bloc had held its last meeting on June 8 and had announced that they propose to meet next in Hyderabad in August. However, the date of the meeting is yet to be decided.
Article Summary: TMC’s Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’ Brien said that while the session that ended on Thursday belonged to the opposition, it was the protests over the NEET paper leaks at Jantar Mantar by youth that set the pitch for what followed in Parliament. The TMC leader further said that a key takeaway from this session was that the opposition worked in a coordinated way.

Article Title: 2027 UP assembly elections: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
Article Text:
As Mayawati's base shrinks, BJP, SP and Congress intensify fight for Dalit votes in UP

From 206 seats to one: How BSP lost ground

BJP's Dalit outreach gets sharper ahead of 2027

SP’s Dalit outreach

How Samajwadi Party performed when they contested independently

Congress tries to reclaim lost ground

Chandrashekhar Azad adds another claimant

NEW DELHI: Dalit politics in Uttar Pradesh is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. Not any more. Mayawati’s BSP today is a much weaker force. The last three elections in the state have pushed Mayawati, the four-time chief minister of UP, to the margins of state politics. This has opened up the Dalit space and triggered an interesting scramble among political parties for a slice of the Dalit pie in the 2027 assembly elections.So, we have the BJP playing the name-change game in Bhadohi and organising a 7-month campaign to honour 15th-century saint-poet Sant Ravi Das. Then we have Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav announcing 14 extra seats for the Dalits to cement his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) politics. Congress too is trying to win back voters it lost decades ago. Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, who is trying to consolidate his own space in the state.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards 2027, the question is: if the BSP continues to lose ground, where does Mayawati’s old support base go and which of her rivals stands to gain the most?The BSP’s rise in UP politics was as dramatic as its fall. The party was founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 with the idea of giving Dalits and other marginalized communities an independent voice.Mayawati, who emerged as his political successor, took the BSP to great heights in Uttar Pradesh. Under her leadership, the BSP won a majority on its own in the 2007 assembly elections, winning 206 seats with a vote share of 30.43%.Dalits, who constitute around 21% of UP’s population as per the 2021 census, have for years been the core base of Mayawati’s Bahujan Samaj Party. But that dynamic has now changed.BSP is a much weaker force today. Mayawati has failed to mobilise Dalit support for her BSP in the last two elections in the state, thereby opening up the space for other political contenders. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawati’s dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her party’s vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSP’s influence among Dalits.As Mayawati gears up for the 2027 assembly challenge, she faces an uphill road. The BSP chief has not just lost support of voters, but also control over her party. So, when Mayawati issued a stern message that all the candidates for the upcoming poll will be finalised by her and not by her nephew Akash Anand, it was an indication of the internal tussle in her party.Akash Anand, who has been in and out of Mayawati’s favour in the past, launched the party’s 2027 assembly poll campaign from Sadabad in Hathras this week.Mayawati, who has often been accused of helping the BJP, has ruled out any pre-poll alliance. She has claimed that some candidates have already been finalised for the upcoming assembly elections. Mayawati has asked party cadres to start rebuilding the party and drum up OBC support ahead of the polls. The cadres have apparently been asked to remind people of the party's past governance and convince them that the real benefit and welfare of the OBC community lie with the BSP and its "iron lady government".Mayawati, however, must consider that it will be difficult for the BSP to come back to power only by holding on to its core Dalit vote alone. It will have to recreate the Dalit-OBC combination that originally carried Mayawati to power in Lucknow with a majority of her own.One interesting fallout of BSP’s decline has been the BJP’s aggressive outreach to woo the Dalits. When Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath announced the renaming of Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar last month, he put the BJP right at the middle of the Dalit outreach battle ahead of 2027 polls.The move also revived an old political contest over name-change politics. Mayawati was the one who had renamed Bhadohi as Sant Ravidas Nagar in December 1997. Akhilesh Yadav restored the old name in 2014. Now, by bringing Sant Ravidas Nagar back, Yogi sought to make a bigger political point, accusing the SP of erasing a Dalit symbol while positioning the BJP as a party willing to restore it.Mayawati publicly welcomed the decision, a rare moment of agreement with the ruling party. She was quick, however, to remind voters that it was her government that had changed the district's name in the first place and that the decision was later reversed under Akhilesh.The party realises that Dalit votes are up for grabs and hence is going all out to woo them. The party’s 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan’ appears planned to coincide with assembly elections in two key states, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, early next year.Both these states have a sizeable population of Dalits who play an important role in many constituencies. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (Soneylal) together bagged 63 Scheduled Caste (SC) seats compared to 20 won by the then Samajwadi Party-led opposition alliance. But the 2024 Lok Sabha polls changed the dynamics, with the SP and the Congress winning 43 of the 80 seats in the state and pushing the BJP to make an aggressive outreach. The loss of Faizabad seat to SP's Awadhesh Prasad, a Pasi leader, was particularly significant and gave Akhilesh Yadav fresh ammunition for his PDA pitch.Earlier this year, the Yogi Adityanath government approved the “Dr B R Ambedkar Murti Vikas Yojna" under which Rs 1 crore is to be allocated to each of the state's 403 assembly constituencies for the beautification and development of statues of social reformers.The BJP's efforts to woo Dalits has also been visible in its recent Cabinet expansion. Of the six new ministers inducted into the Yogi government, two were Dalits, Krishna Paswan from the Pasi community and Surendra Singh Daler from the Valmiki community. Three others were from OBC groups. Two non-Yadav OBC ministers were also given independent charge.The BJP's primary task ahead of 2027 would be to hold on to the non-Jatav Dalit support it built over the past decade and prevent a repeat of 2024.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections also showed that the Dalits in UP were ready to back other political parties who wooed them. Dalit support played a key role in the spectacular success of Akhilesh Yadav’s Samajwadi Party, which won 37 seats in 2024.Together with its alliance partner Congress, the INDIA bloc won 43 of the 80 seats in the state, pushing the BJP on the back foot. Akhilesh Yadav, who has centred his politics around PDA (Pichhde, Dalits and Aplasankhyaks), gained from his Dalit outreach in the 2024 elections. His Samajwadi Party fielded two Dalit candidates from general seats. While one of them went on to win the all-important Faizabad seat, the other lost by just 10,585 votes to the BJP in Meerut.Little wonder, in the run-up to the 2027 assembly elections, Akhilesh has already announced plans to field 14 Dalit candidates from general seats. Uttar Pradesh has 84 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and two for Scheduled Tribes. With 14 more candidates on general seats, the total tally of reserved candidates for SP will increase to 100. This will help reinforce his message to the Dalits in line with his PDA politics. The move will also help the SP shed the narrative of being a Muslim-Yadav party. Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that Dalits would now play a 'central role' in Congress. Before Mayawati and the BSP built their massive Dalit vote bank in the 1990s, Congress was the primary choice for Uttar Pradesh's Dalits. For nearly three decades after that, Congress was almost pushed out of UP politics.Rahul Gandhi has started his road to the UP election by acknowledging that the party had failed to take the right steps for the community in the 1980s and 1990s. He even praised Kanshi Ram for bringing Dalits together and giving the community a sense of confidence.Rahul has also made the Constitution a regular part of his social justice pitch. He is often seen carrying the red book of the Constitution while warning that constitutional rights and reservation are under threat. He has repeatedly invoked BR Ambedkar in the same pitch, asserting that Congress wants to position itself as a guardian of the Constitution.The party has also put a Dalit leader in charge of Uttar Pradesh. Rajendra Pal Gautam, who heads the Congress’s Scheduled Castes Department, has been appointed UP in-charge ahead of the 2027 polls. Interestingly, Gautam had also made an unsuccessful attempt to meet Mayawati at her Lucknow residence earlier this year.Whether the party will be able to translate this outreach into votes remains to be seen.Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, whose 2024 victory from Nagina made him a prominent figure in UP’s Dalit politics. Unlike BJP, SP or Congress, Azad is trying to build an independent space outside the BSP. His challenge now is to take that appeal beyond one constituency and build an organisation strong enough to matter across the state in 2027.That is what makes the coming assembly election in Uttar Pradesh interesting. For decades, politics in Uttar Pradesh has revolved around caste. Political parties build their electoral strategies around social coalitions, loyalty of communities and traditional vote base.Mayawati may no longer command the Dalit vote the way she once did, but that vote bank has not disappeared. It simply has more claimants. And in 2027, where those voters eventually move could make a significant difference.
Article Summary: Dalit politics in Uttar Pradesh is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. But that dynamic has now changed. BSP is a much weaker force today.

Article Title: Over 11k Indian workers died in Saudi, UAE each in 2021-25, MEA informs Parliament
Article Text:
Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries

Saudi Arabia and the UAE accounted for the vast majority of Indian worker fatalities across Gulf countries from 2021 to 2025 - over 71% of total recorded deaths. According to figures released by ministry of external affairs (MEA) in Parliament on Thursday, Saudi Arabia topped the list with 11,923 deaths, and the UAE was second with 11,489 fatalities. Kuwait reported 3,890 deaths, Oman 2,457, Qatar 1,548 and Bahrain 1,206 deaths. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with Covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.From 2022 onwards, while countries like Bahrain and Qatar registered lower death counts, Saudi Arabia and the UAE recorded upward trends through 2024-2025. Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries, with the UAE alone accounting for 4.5 million Indians.
Article Summary: Saudi Arabia and the UAE accounted for the vast majority of Indian worker fatalities across Gulf countries from 2021 to 2025. Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with Covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.

Article Text:

JAMMU: Thirty-five years after an explosion rocked Jammu Tawi railway station, killing three people and leaving 18 others wounded, Govt Railway Police (GRP) Jammu Thursday claimed it arrested Altaf Hussain Sheikh, a fugitive terrorist wanted in the case.A native of Marhama, Bijbehara, in south Kashmir’s Anantnag district, Sheikh went underground after the April 2, 1991, attack along with two co-accused even as their accomplice, Aman Ullah Khan, was caught that day. Charged under relevant provisions of the stringent Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, Explosive Substances Act, and Ranbir Penal Code, Sheikh managed to evade arrest for three-and-a-half decades by concealing his identity and assuming another, a GRP spokesperson said.During the investigation, the fugitive terrorists were declared “absconders” by court. “In the past two years, GRP Jammu intensified the hunt for the trio. A team verified Sheikh’s identity by examining his residential details and other particulars and found that he had established himself as a successful businessman in Bijbehara,” the spokesperson said.Sheikh was produced before the TADA court Thursday for further legal proceedings, the spokesperson added.
Article Summary: Altaf Hussain Sheikh is a fugitive terrorist wanted in the case. He went underground after the April 2, 1991, attack along with two co-accused. Sheikh managed to evade arrest for three-and-a-half decades. He was produced before the TADA court Thursday for further legal proceedings.

Article Title: From erotic fantasy to Indian identity, a famous Italian calendar finds a new story
Article Text:
Behind-the-scenes image featuring Avani Rai (left) during the Pirelli Calendar shoot in Delhi I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti

One half of the 2027 Pirelli Calendar features Indian celebrities photographed by Norwegian photographer Sølve Sundsbø I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti

In 1966, a photograph of a woman in underwear arrived at the Vatican. The fashion imagery might seem rather tame by today's standards, but it was enough to provoke an official complaint from the Holy See to an Italian tire company called Pirelli. The Milan-based tire manufacturer had just begun producing these exclusive, high-fashion calendars, simply called 'The Cal', as a trade gift for its top clients — the idea being to give VIPs something a cut above the cheap pin-up calendars that were standard fare in garages and tire shops at the time.But the condemnation had the opposite effect. Rather than suppressing the calendar, it generated enormous publicity, transforming a niche corporate giveaway into one of the world's most coveted cultural status symbols. Within a few years, the calendar became less a marketing gimmick and more an annual referendum on where European ideas of beauty, sex and provocation stood. Over the decades, figures from Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford and Kate Moss to Penélope Cruz, Serena Williams and Yoko Ono have been framed within its pages by some of the world's most influential photographers. But sixty-two years and a great many controversies later, the most recent edition of that same calendar is shot not on a Mediterranean beach or a Manhattan studio, but in the forts and villages of Rajasthan and the mean streets of Old Delhi, even featuring everyday barbers and artisans.The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country, built around the idea of Indian identity. So alongside glamorous portraits of celebrities like television host and author Padma Lakshmi, actress Aditi Rao Hydari, sitarist Anoushka Shankar and supermodel Bhavitha Mandava are some 200 ordinary Indians, from dancers and street artists to musicians and craftspeople.The project began as a collaboration between Norwegian photographer Sølve Sundsbø and Raghu Rai, modern India's most celebrated photojournalist known for chronicling the country's many faces and contradictions over several decades. Rai died in April shortly after the project began. His daughter, photographer Avani Rai, stepped in to complete it and in doing so changed its direction. What had been conceived as a studio shoot moved outdoors into the neighbourhoods her father spent his career documenting, from Kinari Bazar and Yamuna Ghat to the streets of Old Delhi.When asked how a project like the Pirelli Calendar sits alongside her reportage-driven practice, Avani, speaking to TOI, gently rejects the premise of the question. Genre, she argues, describes where a photograph ends up, not how it is made. What remains constant, whether in documentary work or a fashion commission, is the attempt to stay honest to what is in front of the camera. "Curiosity, presence and empathy are not specific to one genre of photography. The Pirelli Calendar asked me to bring those values into a different context. I wasn’t interested in making images that simply looked beautiful. I wanted them to feel alive. To hold the same emotional honesty that I search for in every photograph I make," says Avani whose mother, conservation architect Gurmeet Rai, also appears in the calendar.Even to this day, The Cal's physical copies are not sold publicly; Pirelli limits production to roughly 20,000 copies annually and they are sent as corporate gifts to monarchs, CEOs, prime ministers, top celebrities, fashion icons and the like.But why India? Sundsbø says it was a long-held ambition within Pirelli. His contribution came from a very different vantage point—that of an outsider conscious of his own limitations. "The fact that Avani and Raghu Rai’s images would be one half of the Calendar enabled me to concentrate on portraits. That's a smaller and more realistic task for a visitor than capturing the whole soul of a nation.I didn’t try to decide what “Indianness” should mean. Especially not as the guest that I am. I tried to cast people I admire, women who have inspirational talent," says Sundsbø.The edition also marks the first time Pirelli has commissioned two photographers to share a calendar. What makes the India edition notable is not simply that it swaps eroticism for cultural identity; the calendar has been moving in that direction for years. Rather, it is the first edition shaped by two intertwined perspectives: an outsider looking in and a daughter completing her father's final project in the streets he loved."I used to think inheritance was about continuing someone’s work. Now I think it’s about continuing their way of being in the world. The patience they lived with. The integrity they carried. The generosity with which they met people. Those are the things that survive," says Avani."Completing the calendar gave me a sense of continuity. It wasn’t about recreating him or holding onto the past. I understood that what he had really left me wasn’t an archive or even a body of work. It was a practice of being alive to the world," she adds.
Article Summary: The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country. The project began as a collaboration between Norwegian photographer Sølve Sundsbø and Raghu Rai, modern India's most celebrated photojournalist.

Article Title: Watch: When gunman tried to assassinate Sukhbir Badal at Golden Temple in 2024
Article Text:
On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked inside the Golden Temple during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Sukhbir Singh Badal’s Thursday attack in Nanded marks the second serious attempt on the Shiromani Akali Dal leader’s life. The SAD leader was also attacked two years ago at the Golden Temple when a gunman opened fire at him while Badal was serving religious punishment at the shrine.On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked at the entrance of the temple, where he was seated in a wheelchair because of his fractured leg, during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht. Video footage from the incident shows the moment the attacker overpowered him within seconds.The footage showed him dressed in a blue sewadar uniform. He was stationed at the temple entrance as part of the punishment pronounced by the Akal Takht over alleged misconduct during his tenure from 2007 to 2017.As Badal sat with a placard around his neck, a man who was later identified as Narayan Singh Chaura approached him and opened fire. The attempt, however, was foiled almost immediately.In the clip, right after the gunman pulled out the weapon, an alert sewadar, believed to be a volunteer associated with an Akali leader, intervened and pushed the assailant’s arm upward as he attempted to fire. The bullet was discharged harmlessly into the air, and the attacker was quickly overpowered by volunteers and others present at the scene.Police personnel stationed at the shrine also moved in and apprehended Chaura on the spot. Confirming the swift response, ADCP Harpal Singh said, “No one was injured in the attack.”It was not long after the attempted attack that other sewadars present at the scene assembled together to create a human shield around Badal.Despite the dramatic shooting attempt, Badal remained calm.Still seated in his wheelchair, he continued performing his duties as a sewadar, holding a spear and staying at the temple entrance after the assailant had been detained.In a separate clip, the shooter could be seen being overpowered by the crowd. The people holding the man can be heard asking him his motive for opening fire on the SAD leader.The religious punishment had been announced on December 2, 2024, by Sikh high priests for Badal and other Akali leaders in connection with incidents of sacrilege and the pardon granted to controversial Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. The tankhah was part of a reconciliation process led by Sikh religious authorities to address long-standing grievances within the community.With Wednesday’s attack once again putting security arrangements at the Golden Temple under scrutiny, the earlier firing incident has returned to focus as a reminder that this was not the first time Sukhbir Singh Badal was targeted while performing religious service at Sikhism’s holiest shrine.
Article Summary: On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked inside the Golden Temple during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht. Video footage from the incident shows the moment the attacker overpowered him within seconds. Other sewadars present at the scene assembled together to create a human shield around Badal.

Article Title: Justice Yashwant Varma cash-at-home row: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?
Article Text:
. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varma’s removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President”. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.
Article Summary: Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings. As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President’

Article Title: Ready for long debate, can answer any question but opposition doesn’t want it: Amit Shah
Article Text:
Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.

BJP

accuses Rahul of ‘anti-democracy, anarchic’ mindset

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday flung a challenge at the opposition for a comprehensive debate over police action during the anti-NEET protests in Delhi on July 20, saying he was ready for a 24-hour-long debate in Parliament at an hour’s notice over their charge of police excesses against protesting students. He said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.“If they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day. I am ready to answer any question. But they (opposition) do not want debate to take place in Parliament. Let the people decide who is running away,” he told the media a day before the end of the monsoon session, which has been marred by the opposition’s disruptions over a host of issues. Soon after, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said govt could even push for the session’s extension if the opposition wants.Shah said while the opposition had initially demanded his statement, govt had gone beyond it by agreeing to an extensive debate followed by his reply so that people could decide who was right and who was wrong.Amit Shah’s aggressive counter was seconded by a host of senior BJP functionaries, with party president Nitin Nabin saying the conduct of Rahul and the entire opposition was reflective of their “anarchic and anti-democracy” mindset.“The entire session is about to be over but they did not agree to a serious discussion over any issue,” he said, accusing them of running away after govt’s offer of a debate.With INDIA bloc MPs frequently accusing him of “running away” from Parliament, Shah hit back and said he was regularly in his chamber in the House. When the opposition was not letting the House function, what was the point of him going there, he asked.Expressing anguish at his opponents’ jibes like “lapata” (missing) and “bhagora” (fugitive) for him, Shah said these terms were being used only recently in parliamentary discourse.The minister later wrote to the Speaker, urging him to reach out to the opposition so that a discussion could begin. “You can allot as much time you think appropriate with mutual agreement. I want to participate in the discussion and I’m ready to answer every question of the opposition,” he said, adding that a solution to any issue in democracy emerged from dialogue and discussion.Congress had normalised disruption in Parliament, he said, adding a party which governed India for decades had fallen to such a low that it did not want discussion in the House.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him. He said if they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day.

Sophie Cunningham picked up an unlikely ally this week when actor Hugh Laurie publicly backed her stance on transgender athletes in women's sports. The Indiana Fever guard has spent weeks defending comments she made about protecting girls and women in competition, and Laurie's entry into the debate on Aug. 11 pushed the conversation into the entertainment world.The exchange started with a dry post about basketball and ended with Laurie stating his position directly, then naming Cunningham by name.Laurie opened the discussion on Aug. 9 with an observation about how rare it is for a man to reach seven feet tall, framing professional basketball as a sport where almost everyone is unusually built. Writer and comedian Graham Linehan pushed back, calling that approach "cowardly" in a post he later deleted, and asked Laurie to state his views outright.Laurie did not soften his answer. He wrote, "I don't believe men should compete against women," and made clear he thought his position had already been obvious. When Linehan pressed further and asked if he backed Cunningham specifically, Laurie confirmed it, “You started it. ‘Cowardly’ to ‘f*ck off’ is the going rate of exchange around here. No new eligibility rules came out of the meeting. The league said afterward, "There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA," while also condemning efforts to use the issue to demean people.The 2026 collective bargaining agreement limits WNBA rosters to players who are women but does not define the term further, and no transgender woman has played in the league. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve has argued for a more inclusive approach, and Storm center Stefanie Dolson has voiced support for transgender rights.The players' union has said it wants to avoid turning athletes into political pawns. Colon died on August 13, 2026, aged 33, nearly 11 years after facing Terrel Williams at EagleBank Arena in Virginia. One question that has stayed around the fight is whether Williams ever apologized to Colon or his parents, Richard and Nieves Colon, for the punches to the back of his head. There is no public record of a formal apology. Williams has, however, spoken about his regret, said he prays for Colon and described how the fight changed his own life.Williams has never publicly said that he formally apologized to Prichard Colon or his parents. I don’t wish nothing but peace and health for that man. It’s been hard on me, too. I didn’t want that to happen to him. I was just trying to win a fight. My life changed that night, and it will never be the same.”That was not the same as a direct apology to the Colon family.The Washington Post also reported in 2019 that Williams wanted to speak with the family but believed that conversation would not happen. He said the incident had affected both his and Colon’s lives.Williams had also tried to visit Colon in the hospital after the fight, according to The Washington Post. He said he was advised against making the visit. The report said Williams knew Nieves Colon blamed him for what happened to her son and that he continued to pray for Prichard.The family’s anger remained. In 2017, Richard and Nieves Colon filed a lawsuit seeking more than $50 million over the injuries suffered during the fight, naming ringside physician Richard Ashby and the promoters.Colon and Williams met on October 17, 2015. Colon entered the fight with a 16-0 record, including 13 knockouts. During the bout, Colon complained about punches to the back of his head, known as rabbit punches.Referee Joe Cooper deducted a point from Williams in the seventh round after one such punch. But more punches to the back of Colon’s head followed, including one later in the fight that was not called a foul.The ninth round became the turning point. Williams knocked Colon down twice. A misunderstanding in Colon’s corner then led to the fighter being disqualified before the 10th round. After returning to his dressing room, Colon became dizzy, vomited and eventually lost consciousness. He died on August 13, 2026.Williams’ role in the incident was also investigated by Virginia’s Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation. The investigation did not result in disciplinary action against Williams, referee Joe Cooper or ringside doctor Richard Ashby.So, while Williams has repeatedly expressed regret and said he wanted peace and health for Colon, there is no public evidence that he ever made a formal apology to Colon’s parents. Article Title: Inspiring story on fatherhood: "Part of being a great father is being a great example of doing what it takes to take care of your family" - How Tom Brady's children became the heart of his life after
Article Text:
Tom Brady's view of what makes a great father

Tom Brady's children watched the person behind the NFL legend

Why football success was never the whole story for Tom Brady

Tom Brady is building a legacy beyond football

For much of his career, Tom Brady was defined by championships, records and an almost relentless commitment to football. Away from the stadium, however, another role has always carried a different kind of weight. As a father of three, Brady says his children have watched not only what he achieved, but how he worked for it. That lesson, he believes, may be one of his most meaningful legacies.Brady recently offered a personal look at fatherhood while reflecting on what life means beyond professional success. His message was not simply about spending time with children. Instead, he focused on the example parents set through their everyday choices."I think part of being a great father is being a great example of doing what it takes to take care of your family," he explained. "I chose to do it by playing football."For Brady, football was more than a career. It was also the way he showed his children the value of commitment, discipline and responsibility. The quarterback spent years building a routine around training, preparation and competition, often under enormous pressure."My dedication to the sport, the hours of practice, the moments when I was laser focused — those were times when I believe I was doing the best possible thing for my family and my kids, by prioritizing my profession and teaching, by example, what it takes to be really good at your job, what it takes to follow through on commitments, what it takes to be a great teammate; and showing them, also by example, that work is a big part of all of our lives. "That perspective adds another layer to Brady's famous career. The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star spent much of his adult life chasing excellence. His children were growing up while he was doing it.Rather than seeing those years only as sacrifices, Brady now views them as opportunities to demonstrate what dedication looks like.Brady is the father of three children. He shares his eldest son, John "Jack" Edward Thomas, with actress Bridget Moynahan. He shares daughter Vivian Lake and son Benjamin Rein with former wife Gisele Bündchen.His children have also experienced a childhood far removed from the ordinary. They watched their father compete on football's biggest stages, including Super Bowls, while also seeing the less glamorous side of professional sport. Early mornings, long practices, travel and recovery were all part of the picture.Brady believes those details matter."Remember, your children are watching everything. They see what you do in every aspect of your life and how you do it," he wrote. "Reading bedtime stories and helping them with homework are not the only ways to be a great parent."That does not mean Brady considers traditional parenting moments unimportant. His point is broader. Children learn from consistency. They notice how adults respond when things go wrong, whether promises are kept and how seriously they approach their responsibilities.For an athlete who built his reputation on preparation, those lessons naturally became part of his parenting philosophy.Brady also drew a clear line between sporting achievement and being a successful father."And neither is winning Super Bowls or MVPs," he continued. "Being a great football player didn’t make me a great dad, but how I became a great player certainly had an impact — from showing up day in and day out, to doing whatever it took to get better, be successful, be a role model, and to provide."It is a striking distinction from one of the most decorated careers in NFL history. Brady won seven Super Bowl titles and collected multiple individual honours, but his own definition of success as a parent does not rest on those achievements.Instead, he points towards the habits that helped him reach those heights.That message becomes especially relevant now that football no longer controls every part of his schedule. Brady has been able to devote more attention to family experiences, including holidays and trips with his children.His social media posts have offered glimpses of those moments. He has shared photographs with Jack, Vivian and Benjamin during family travels, including a European summer filled with sightseeing, time on the water and opportunities to experience different cultures.He also celebrated quieter moments. One photograph showed Vivian enjoying time in the water during a trip to Spain, prompting her proud father to call her his "little mermaid."The former quarterback's approach to fatherhood shows how dramatically the meaning of legacy can change after a sporting career.For decades, Brady's legacy was measured in wins, championships and statistics. Now, his own words suggest that the lessons he passes to his children matter just as much.His three children have seen the famous quarterback at work, but they have also seen a father who values preparation, persistence and responsibility. Those qualities can remain long after the final whistle.Brady's message is ultimately simple. Being present as a parent does not only mean being physically beside your children every moment. It also means giving them something to learn from.His football career provided the platform, but fatherhood gave those lessons a deeper purpose. Whether his children follow his path into sports or choose completely different careers, Brady appears to hope they carry forward the same principles: work hard, honour commitments, keep improving and show up for the people who matter.For a man who spent much of his life trying to become the best quarterback possible, that may be the most personal measure of success. His trophies tell the story of Tom Brady the athlete. His children, and the example he hopes to leave them, tell the story of Tom Brady the father.
Article Summary: NFL legend Tom Brady is the father of three children. Brady says his children have watched not only what he achieved, but how he worked for it. The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star spent much of his adult life chasing excellence. Brady has been able to devote more attention to family, including holidays with his children.

Article Title: What happens to Carter Hart now? Hockey star’s ban upheld after acquittal, 4 players still suspended
Article Text:

What happens to Carter Hart now?

Four players were acquitted in court, but their Hockey Canada suspensions remain in place

What Hart's 2028 World Cup eligibility could mean

Carter Hart will remain barred from Hockey Canada programs through November 2027, even though a criminal court acquitted him of se*ual assault last year. An independent appeal board upheld that suspension on Wednesday, closing out a disciplinary process that ran separately from the courtroom case and outlasted it by more than a year.The ruling covers five players from Canada's 2018 World Junior team. Four remain suspended on staggered timelines, while a fifth was reinstated immediately. None of it affects their ability to play in the NHL, which conducted its own investigation and cleared all five to sign contracts again last year.Carter Hart, the Vegas Golden Knights goaltender, cannot participate in any Hockey Canada-sanctioned program until Nov. 10, 2027. That date falls just months before the 2028 World Cup of Hockey, the tournament's first edition since 2016, which sets up a real question about whether he could eventually wear the Maple Leaf again.His NHL path looks different. Hart signed a two-year, $4 million deal with Vegas last October and helped the Golden Knights reach the 2026 Stanley Cup Final before losing to the Carolina Hurricanes in six games. He posted a .909 save percentage and 2.56 goals-against average across 22 playoff appearances, numbers that outpaced every other Canadian goaltender in the postseason.The players, Hart, Michael McLeod, Dillon Dube, Cal Foote and Alex Formenton, were accused of se*ually assaulting a woman in a London, Ontario hotel room in 2018. All five were acquitted in July 2025 after a judge found the accuser's testimony not credible. Hockey Canada's own investigation reached a different conclusion on conduct, and the appeal board upheld it this week.Formenton was reinstated immediately. Foote's suspension runs through November 2026, Hart's through 2027, Dube's through 2028, and McLeod's through 2030. Officials have not explained why the timelines differ. Any of the four will also face an enhanced screening process, including a third-party review of the original findings, before Hockey Canada would consider them for a future roster.Canada's secretary of sport, Adam van Koeverden, framed the case as a turning point for the sport. "This case started a national conversation about safe sport," he said following the ruling, pointing to reforms Hockey Canada has made since the allegations first surfaced.Hart's on-ice case for a future recall is real. His regular-season numbers with Vegas last season were modest, an .891 save percentage over 18 starts, but he was working his way back after more than a year away from competitive hockey. The playoff run changed the conversation, and rival Canadian goaltenders like Colorado's Scott Wedgewood never matched his output.Selecting him would still be a hard call. The 2018 case drew national outrage, and Hockey Canada has spent years trying to rebuild trust through programs like Abuse Free Sport. The NHL, in its own July 2025 statement on the players, called their alleged conduct "unacceptable" even after the acquittals.Hart has kept his public comments focused on hockey rather than the case itself. "I'm just excited to move forward," he told reporters after signing with Vegas last fall.Whether that focus extends to a Team Canada jersey in 2028 depends on decisions Hockey Canada has not yet had to make.
Article Summary: Carter Hart will remain barred from Hockey Canada programs through November 2027. An independent appeal board upheld that suspension on Wednesday. The ruling covers five players from Canada's 2018 World Junior team. Four remain suspended on staggered timelines, while a fifth was reinstated immediately.

She is seeking more than $25,000 in damages, along with the return of her property and punitive damages, according to court documents reported by TMZ on August 13, 2026.The lawsuit comes after their relationship ended in June 2025. Holly and Brown have two children together, and she says the problems began when she left their Ohio home and could not collect everything she owned. Brown denies wrongdoing and disputes her version of events.Orlando Brown Jr.’s ex, Holly says she lived with Brown and their two children at his Ohio home until their June 2025 breakup. According to her lawsuit, Brown forced her out without notice, leaving her unable to collect all of her personal belongings.She claims the property did not stay in one place. Some of her belongings, she says, ended up in Oklahoma and Kansas City. Holly alleges that Brown then blocked her efforts to retrieve them, including attempts to collect property from a storage unit.The dispute continued into Jan. 2026. Holly says she went to Brown’s Ohio home with police to collect her belongings. She claims Brown knew why she had arrived but refused to answer the door.Holly alleges Brown acted out of “anger and spite” following their breakup and her decision to move with their children back to Oregon. She also claims he acted with “ill will or a spirit of revenge.”She is asking for more than $25,000 in damages, the return of her property and punitive damages. TMZ reports that Holly filed the case as a civil theft lawsuit.Brown strongly disputes those claims. He says Holly came to his home unannounced after he had asked her not to come there. He also argues that she abandoned the property after their separation and has asked the court to dismiss the lawsuit with prejudice.The lawsuit follows a relationship that had been public for several years. Brown and Holly, who was previously known publicly as Holly Luyah, began sharing their relationship publicly around 2019. They later started a family and have two sons together.Their second child, Sonny, was born in December 2023. CBS Pittsburgh reported that Brown was in Pittsburgh preparing to play the Steelers when Holly went into labour early, and he watched the birth through FaceTime before playing that game. Their relationship ultimately ended in June 2025, according to Holly’s lawsuit.Orlando Brown’s response puts the focus on what happened after the breakup. He denies that he wrongfully kept Holly’s property and says she came to his home without an appointment after he had told her not to.His legal position also challenges Holly’s claim that he deliberately kept her belongings from her. Brown argues that she abandoned the property when she left following their split. He is asking the court to dismiss the case with prejudice.That means the court has two conflicting accounts of the same dispute. Holly says Brown prevented her from getting her property because of anger over the breakup. Brown says she left the items behind and later came to his home without his permission.Currently, Holly’s accusations remain allegations. There has been no court finding that Brown committed civil theft or acted with ill will, and Brown continues to deny wrongdoing. The lawsuit will determine what happens next.
Article Summary: Holly Means, the Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle’s ex-girlfriend, has sued him over property she says he has refused to return. She is seeking more than $25,000 in damages, along with the return of her property and punitive damages. Brown denies wrongdoing and disputes her version of events.

Article Title: Who were they? Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina’s secret wedding had just five people present with zero outside guests
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina’s secret wedding had just five guests after couple kept ceremony completely private

Ronaldo and Georgina kept the ceremony intimate

The five children were the centre of the guest list

Hundreds of fans had already gone looking for the wrong wedding

A decade-long relationship ends with a quiet ceremony

I Am Georgina

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez chose to keep their wedding almost entirely away from the public eye, and the first details emerging from the ceremony suggest they succeeded. After nearly a decade together, the couple reportedly married in a private civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, with the occasion centred not on footballers, celebrities or a large circle of friends, but on their family.The scale of the ceremony is particularly striking given the extraordinary attention surrounding their relationship in the days before they finally confirmed they were married.Ronaldo and Rodriguez married in Cascais on August 11, bringing an end to years of speculation over when they would formalise their relationship.The couple announced the marriage themselves with a photograph of their wedding bands on Instagram, accompanied by the simple caption “C❤️G.” A representative for Ronaldo subsequently confirmed that the ceremony was held in Cascais and described it as an “intimate and private” occasion.The secrecy surrounding the wedding had fuelled considerable speculation in the buildup, with reports and rumours ranging from the guest list and wedding arrangements to how much the couple might spend on the ceremony.However, there has still been no definitive public account of the wedding’s guest list or overall arrangements.The closest indication came from Ronaldo’s representative, who told the Daily Mail that the ceremony was “a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.” The representative said: “Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.”If that account is accurate, and the five children were the only people present apart from Ronaldo and Rodriguez, it would mean the ceremony had no outside guests, making the already private wedding even smaller than many of the rumours surrounding it had suggested.Ronaldo and Rodriguez have five children between them, with two being Rodriguez's biological children and the other three being Ronaldo's children from before his relationship with Rodriguez began.Their presence meant the ceremony remained firmly centred on the family the couple have built together rather than becoming a high-profile celebrity event.That privacy appears to have been deliberate. There had been no confirmed details about the ceremony beforehand, leaving supporters and the media to speculate about everything from the location to the scale of the wedding.Instead, Ronaldo and Rodriguez reportedly chose a civil ceremony in Cascais and revealed the marriage only afterwards.The contrast with the speculation surrounding their wedding could hardly have been greater.Only days before Ronaldo and Rodriguez confirmed their marriage, attention had been focused on Funchal Cathedral in Madeira.Reports had claimed the couple would marry there on August 8, prompting hundreds of fans, journalists and well-wishers to gather outside the cathedral in Ronaldo's hometown.The wedding taking place at the cathedral belonged to another Portuguese couple, Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira, rather than Ronaldo and Rodriguez. The extraordinary confusion left the genuine wedding location completely out of the spotlight.That episode also gave Ronaldo the opportunity to see the lighter side of the speculation. When footage and photographs circulated showing crowds waiting outside the church for him and Rodriguez, he reacted with laughing emojis on social media.The real wedding was subsequently revealed to have taken place in Cascais, rather than Madeira, and to have been considerably more private than the crowds gathered in Funchal had anticipated.Ronaldo and Rodriguez began their relationship in 2016, when Rodriguez was working at a Gucci store in Madrid.Rodriguez later recalled in her Netflix seriesthat Ronaldo would sometimes collect her from work, including once in a Bugatti, despite her arriving at the store by bus.She left the job later that year after fans began gathering outside the shop, and the couple made their first public appearance together at The Best FIFA Football Awards in January 2017.They subsequently built a family together, with Ronaldo's twins Mateo and Eva born via surrogacy in June 2017 and Rodriguez giving birth to their daughter Alana Martina later that year.Ronaldo had previously made clear that he intended to marry Rodriguez after the 2026 World Cup, but the couple gave the public no reliable indication of the ceremony's actual timing or location.That secrecy continued right up to the end.After the wedding, Ronaldo and Rodriguez were seen together at Lisbon's Humberto Delgado Airport, accompanied by their children. According to Portuguese media, they entered through a VIP access point, with Saudi Arabia believed to be their likely destination.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez married in Cascais on August 11. The couple announced the marriage themselves with a photograph of their wedding bands on Instagram, accompanied by the simple caption “C❤️G.” A representative for Ronaldo subsequently confirmed that the ceremony was held in the Portuguese city. Ronaldo and Rodriguez have five children between them, with two being Rodriguez's biological children and the other three being Ronaldo's.

Article Title: ‘Gambhir a fantastic coach’: Gary Kirsten backs under-fire India coach to deliver
Article Text:
File Pic: Gary Kirsten and Gautam Gambhir (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: India may be staring at the possibility of another setback in their World Test Championship campaign and that has increased the antagonism that cricket fans in India have towards head coach Gautam Gambhir . However, on Thursday, Gambhir found support from an old ally. Sri Lanka coach Gary Kirsten threw his weight behind the underfire India head coach, insisting that the former opener’s coaching credentials speak for themselves during a virtual media interaction.Kirsten, a former left-handed opener who coached India from 2008-11, cited Gambhir’s coaching record and said, “He’s a fantastic coach. He’s had incredible success. He has won a T20 World Cup (2026) and the ICC Champions Trophy (2025). He’s also had success in the IPL (Gambhir was the team mentor for 2024 IPL champs Kolkata Knight Riders). His record speaks for itself. I really enjoyed working with him when he was a player. He’s a smart cricketer and I knew he’d have success as coach.”Gambhir played under Kirsten when the South African was with the Indian team. He later coached South Africa (2011-13) and served as Pakistan’s head coach in white-ball cricket for six months in 2024.“It was a great three years and a privileged one to work with Indian players,” Kirsten said. “There was a lot of skill in that dressing room. What I appreciated was that they accepted me into their space and felt I could add value.I’ve approached the Sri Lankan role with the same seriousness.”Lately, India have shown a tendency to struggle against quality spin but Kirsten refused to reveal whether Sri Lanka would specifically target that weakness.Instead, he stressed that the hosts were focused on executing their own skills rather than obsessing over opponents.“We would like to bring all our skills into the game, not just spin,” he specified. “Whether you’re a seamer or a spinner, if you’re executing your skills properly, you’ll be in the game. We’ve done our homework on India and identified areas we may be able to exploit, but cricket unfolds session by session and you adapt accordingly.”The South African chose to be diplomatic when asked about India’s recent batting issues against spin. Instead, he kept steering the conversation back to Sri Lanka’s own preparation. “I’m not here to judge the Indian team,” he said. “They are a quality side with tremendous depth. Our responsibility is to make sure we’re ready, both in terms of skill execution and strategy. The focus remains on our strengths.”He also played down suggestions that Sri Lanka’s plans would revolve solely around left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya, whose remarkable record in Galle has earned him the nickname ‘King of Galle’. Jayasuriya has claimed 125 wickets in just 23 Tests, including 81 at the venue. “He’s a world-class bowler and he’s had great success at home,” Kirsten said. “But we don’t build our bowling strategy around one player. Every bowler has a role to play. It’s obviously great to have him in the mix though.”An unapologetic Test cricket-tragic who played in 101 Tests for the Proteas, Kirsten said he preferred longer Test series. “I’m a Test match purist. I love Test cricket. And my personal belief is that every country gets to play at least 10 Tests a year. I was very fortunate to be part of a South African team and to play over 100 Tests over a period of 11 years, which means you’ve got to play somewhere around 10 a year. There are challenges in the modern schedule, but it’s always great when your main Test-playing nations get to play a lot of Test cricket,” said the 58-year-old.Kirsten also welcomed Sri Lanka Cricket’s decision to allow free entry for spectators during the series, saying fuller stadiums create a far better experience. “It’s better to have people in the stadiums than no one,” he said. “I don’t know all the business implications, but from a cricket perspective it’s wonderful.”(Watch the India-Sri Lanka Test series live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV)
Article Summary: Sri Lanka coach Gary Kirsten throws his weight behind India head coach Gautam Gambhir. Kirsten, a former left-handed opener, coached India from 2008-11. Sri Lanka will take on India in a three-Test series starting in Galle.

Article Title: Intrigue around the Galle pitch but India likely to opt for the safe route
Article Text:
Indian players warm up during a training session ahead of the first Test cricket match against Sri Lanka at Galle International Stadium in Galle, Sri Lanka, on Thursday. (ANI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com in Galle:

If you bat first, make sure you go big. And if you bowl first, get the ball in the right area. So those disciplines are going to be important. Morne Morkel

Galle: From front, India's Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sarfaraz Khan, Dhruv Jurel, vice captain KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal during a practice session ahead of the first test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Galle. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak) (PTI08_13_2026_000559B)

Galle: India's Kuldeep Yadav, front, and captain Shubman Gill during a practice session ahead of the first test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Galle. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak) (PTI08_13_2026_000340B)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two days before the Test, there has been an unusual intrigue around the playing surface. Word from both camps is that it isn't the usual strip rolled out at Galle and may not turn as sharply as everyone expected before the series opener. It doesn't look like a dry, raging turner, and generous watering on Thursday suggests there are no attempts to crack it open on the opening day itself.Recent history suggests that for the first couple of days, Galle is a batting paradise, with gradual turn offered as the game progresses. Those who have seen it up close observed that it is a "good wicket," and India bowling coach Morne Morkel emphasised that "something will start to happen" as the match progresses."It looked like a good surface. And I think as the Test match will go on, something will start to happen. We've prepared basically for all that can come our way. And like I said, for us, it's more about the mental challenge now, facing these conditions, batting time, bowling those spells, and getting the ball in the right area," said Morkel during a media interaction."I think it's a good-looking surface on the eye. I'll be slightly surprised if it goes the other way.Traditionally, the first two days belong to the batting side. It's just crucial to get runs on the board. I think that's going to be important to whatever happens with the toss. If you bat first, make sure you go big. And if you bowl first, get the ball in the right area. So those disciplines are going to be important. And then from there, as the day's gone, obviously, assess and then come up with the best options for the day," he added.This leaves India with a crucial riddle to solve. Three spinners or three fast bowlers? As things stand, the former is a more reliable option, primarily because it adds batting depth, something head coach Gautam Gambhir is always averse to compromising. Ravindra Jadeja slots in as the premier all-rounder in the XI, while Mohammed Siraj is the leader of the fast-bowling pack. Kuldeep Yadav remains a no-brainer for this series, leaving two crucial spots to fill. While Prasidh Krishna is expected to narrowly edge Gurnoor Brar for the second pacer spot, Manav Suthar, who had an impressive one-off Test against Afghanistan, will give India that batting cushion at No. 8 and also add variety to the spin attack.If the spin attack remains as expected, it could be a rare instance where the visitors field all left-arm spinners, but this isn't currently bothering the Indian camp. Morkel asserted that all three are different from each other and it isn't a "massive concern" for the group."Kuldeep is an attacking bowler. Jaddu, with his experience and class, we can't look past. I think for us, they're all different in their ways. They're left-arm spinners, but what they do with the ball is slightly more accurate. I don't think it's a massive concern for us. It's just how Shubman is going to use those guys at certain times. In terms of skill, they've got the skill there to get the 20 wickets first," explained Morkel.The last Test at this venue was played between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in June 2025 and saw two 450-plus totals, four hundreds and four half-centuries. The hosts' leading spinner, Prabath Jayasuriya, went wicketless in the first innings, bowling 48 overs without success, and could only pick up one wicket in the second innings as well. Even in the two India A fixtures at the same venue last month, runs were on offer and fast bowlers enjoyed bowling.Gurnoor Brar, in particular, stood out with a 10-wicket haul in the second game.The youngster is very close to earning his Test cap as he continues to bowl with a lot of fire in the nets, and the team management is convinced that he is going to serve Indian cricket for a very long time, provided he remains fit. He hasn't left anything to luck or chance since arriving with the team in the first week of August. He bowled full tilt in Colombo, impressed in the warm-up game at the Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) Ground and bent his back in the first training session in Galle on Thursday. The wait, however, is expected to be slightly longer for the lanky quick.Even though much noise and chatter is expectedly on spin, Galle presents an opportunity for batters from both teams to capitalise on the first two days. For now, the teams will pray for a favourable toss, as the difference between first and fourth innings totals at this venue has been significant in the last few years. Winning the toss, batting first and batting big is going to be the mantra for success at this venue before the spinners can get a nice rip in front of the magnificent Galle Fort.
Article Summary: Two days before the Test, there has been an unusual intrigue around the playing surface. Word from both camps is that it isn't the usual strip rolled out at Galle. It doesn't look like a dry, raging turner, and generous watering on Thursday suggests there are no attempts to crack it open on the opening day.

Article Title: ‘Give him clarity’: Ashwin’s blunt message to Gautam Gambhir over Sarfaraz Khan's India future
Article Text:
Sarfaraz Khan and Gautam Gambhir (Agency Image)
