Sarfaraz Khan’s return to the Indian Test squad has sparked a fresh selection debate ahead of the opening Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with the Mumbai batter competing with Dhruv Jurel for a place in the playing XI.Sarfaraz was brought back into the squad after Sai Sudharsan was ruled out through injury. However, despite his recall, former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes Jurel is more likely to get the nod for the first Test, which begins on August 15.Sarfaraz, 28, has not played for India since the three-Test series against New Zealand (2024). He made a strong statement in the first Test with a 150-run knock, but failed to replicate that performance in the next two matches. He was subsequently left out of the playing XI during the Australia series and was later dropped from the squad altogether.The batter spent more than a year away from the Indian team, with questions surrounding the reasons for his exclusion. One of the reported concerns was his suitability and technique in overseas conditions.Ashwin, however, believes Sarfaraz deserves clarity from the team management if there are doubts about where he fits into India’s plans. According to the former spinner, captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir should clearly communicate Sarfaraz’s role instead of leaving the batter uncertain about his future.“I'll start with Jurel. Sarfaraz came into the squad because of Sai Sudharsan's injury. The messaging is very important for Sarfaraz. If you feel he is a suspect in certain conditions, you need to give him clarity. You need to tell him that he can serve the team in sub-continental conditions," said Ashwin on his YouTube channel ‘Ash Ki Baat’.Ashwin feels Sarfaraz could carve out a significant role for himself in conditions where he is particularly comfortable, especially against spin.“So that way, even Sarfaraz won't waste his time on the rest of the things. He can focus on playing good spin, and he can become the king of the sub-continental conditions. He can build his career. If you feel he cannot work in certain conditions, then communicate that to him,” he added.A place for Sarfaraz in Galle could make sense given his ability to handle spin. The right-hander is comfortable using his feet against spinners and has shown an ability to keep the scoring rate moving by putting pressure on them.His sweep shot is another weapon that could prove useful in Sri Lankan conditions, allowing him to disrupt a spinner’s rhythm and force changes in length.Jurel, meanwhile, has produced mixed returns so far and did not make an impact during India’s warm-up game against SLC XI. That could add another layer to the selection debate, although Ashwin still expects the wicketkeeper-batter to be preferred.Sarfaraz’s experience of batting at No. 5 also means a move to No. 6 would not represent a major adjustment. Much of his domestic career for Mumbai and the West Zone has come in the middle order, where he has accumulated a huge volume of runs.With spin expected to play a major role in Galle, India face an interesting choice between Jurel and Sarfaraz. While Jurel appears to have the edge in Ashwin’s assessment, Sarfaraz’s record against spin and experience in the domestic game could make him a tempting option for the first Test.
Article Summary: Sarfaraz Khan has been recalled to the Indian Test squad for the first Test against Sri Lanka. The Mumbai batter is competing with Dhruv Jurel for a place in the playing XI. Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes JureL is more likely to get the nod.

Article Title: ‘Vaibhav Sooryavanshi doesn’t have that’: Ex-India great explains Rohit Sharma-Virat Kohli’s big edge
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh believes Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma should be allowed to continue their ODI careers and target next year’s World Cup if they retain the desire and fitness to do so, insisting that performance rather than age must determine their place in the team.Speaking to PTI, the 46-year-old former off-spinner weighed in on the ongoing discussion over the future of the two Indian veterans, who are now playing only one format. Harbhajan also revealed that his autobiography is complete and is likely to be released later this year.Harbhajan drew a comparison with Lionel Messi while making the case for Rohit and Kohli . Messi, at 39, led Argentina to the final of the recent football World Cup, producing moments of individual brilliance throughout the tournament.Rohit will be 40 and Kohli 39 when the 2027 ODI World Cup is played in South Africa. Harbhajan believes their age should not become a deciding factor if they continue to perform at the highest level."Whoever the player is, I believe the marker should be performance, not age," Harbhajan said.He feels the expectations surrounding Kohli and Rohit would be significantly greater than those on an inexperienced player such as Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, even though the teenager has already shown the ability to attack international bowlers." Virat may be 39 but if he is still beating those 20-year-old guys on the field, it (his age) doesn't matter. Look at Lionel Messi. At 40 (39), five men fail to stop him. If a player has that kind of fitness and skill where even five opponents can't keep him at bay, then we know that skill always takes precedence," he reasoned.Harbhajan also credited Kohli with changing India's approach towards winning, particularly during his time as captain from 2014-15 onwards. According to the former spinner, Kohli helped the team develop the belief that even seemingly impossible targets could be pursued rather than settling for draws."This change was first brought in by Virat Kohli when he became the captain in 2014-15. Before that we won't think that we can go for a chase of 400 on the final day. Virat told the boys, 'let's at least try. We might lose but if we keep trying one day we will surpass that 400 plus in last innings.'"'If we have to get 10 wickets on last day, we will go for it. The winning mentality and not settle for draw is what Virat Kohli got," he remembered.Kohli's impact, Harbhajan added, extended beyond tactics and results. He believes the former India captain was the biggest driving force behind the team's fitness transformation."But his biggest contribution was bringing in fitness culture. 90 per cent credit for creating the fitness revolution goes to Kohli. My idea of fitness was endurance but Virat made this team believe that if you are fit, you can fly around," Harbhajan pointed out.The former spinner therefore feels India head coach Gautam Gambhir should trust the experience of Rohit and Kohli if they continue to meet the required standards."If I were the coach, my job would be to give them the platform as my expectations from Rohit and Virat would be much higher than what I expect from a Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. These two have that experience. They have experience of 300 games which Sooryavanshi won't have. Yes, a Sooryavanshi can walk in and blast bowlers but Virat and Rohit have the experience," he explained.Harbhajan, who finished his international career with 416 Test wickets and 269 ODI wickets, maintained that fitness and performances should ultimately decide whether the veteran duo remain in contention."Fitness is a priority, and your performance matters. Performance is the ultimate criterion. So if these two score runs and can match the fitness of a Shreyas (Iyer) or a Yashasvi (Jaiswal), then nothing else matters," Harbhajan declared.The former India spinner also believes Rohit and Kohli themselves will know when their bodies and performances indicate that it is time to step away."Rohit and Virat will get their answer from within. You realise when you have reached that phase where you need to call time," he said.Harbhajan officially announced his retirement in December 2021, although his last Test appearance had come much earlier, in 2015 at Galle.
Article Summary: Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh believes Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma should be allowed to continue their ODI careers. The 46-year-old former off- spinner drew a comparison with Lionel Messi while making the case for Rohit and Kohli. He also revealed that his autobiography is complete and is likely to be released later this year.

Article Title: Prichard Colon death at 33: Terrel Williams’ ‘rabbit punches’ revisited as doctor explains Colon’s irreversible brain damage
Article Text:
Prichard Colon death at 33: Terrel Williams’ ‘rabbit punches’ revisited as doctor explains Colon’s irreversible brain damage

What happened to Prichard Colon after the Terrel Williams fight?

Why did Prichard Colon never recover from his brain injury?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Puerto Rican boxer Prichard Colon died at 33 on August 13, nearly 11 years after the 2015 fight that left him with a severe brain injury. Colon suffered repeated punches to the back of his head during his bout with Terrel Williams in Virginia. He later underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain and spent 221 days in a coma. After waking, he remained severely disabled and needed constant care from his family. His death has renewed attention on the injury and why his condition never returned to normal despite years of care.The injury happened during the October 17, 2015, fight at EagleBank Arena in Fairfax, Virginia. Colon complained to referee Joe Cooper about punches to the back of his head, which are illegal in boxing. The World Boxing Council later described these blows, known as rabbit punches, as dangerous because they can damage the area where the spine connects with the brainstem.The fight continued into the ninth round, when Terrel Williams knocked Colon down twice. Colon’s corner then removed his gloves, apparently believing the fight was over. Because he could not answer the bell for the next round, the bout was stopped and Williams was declared the winner by disqualification.After leaving the ring, Colon became dizzy and later vomited and collapsed in the dressing room. He was taken to hospital and underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain.The World Boxing Council said Colon suffered a subdural hematoma and irreversible brain damage from the rabbit punches. He eventually came out of the 221-day coma but was left with severe, permanent problems and could not return to his previous life.Dr. Jason R Williams, a California-based oncologist, explained the possible effect of the injury in a post on X. He wrote: “Those punches landed where the spine meets the brainstem, and the skull barely covers that spot,” Williams wrote on X. “The bleed that started there had nowhere to go. Trapped blood builds pressure. Pressure kills brain tissue.“Brain tissue does not come back. Surgeons saved his life that night, but no treatment in medicine could return what the bleed took. He spent 221 days in a coma and the next decade unable to walk or speak, while his parents cared for him around the clock.“Prichard did what a fighter is supposed to do,” he continued. “He reported the fouls to the one person who could stop them. It didn’t save him. That part has never left me.“Boxing learned from him. In 2016 the WBC put a zero-tolerance rule on those punches and named it after him. Fighters are safer today because of what he lost. Once brain damage runs this deep, we cannot treat our way out of it. Prevention is the only cure.”The WBC later formalised the Prichard Colon Rule, calling for stricter action against rabbit punches.A cause of death for Colon has not been publicly announced. His father, Richard Colon, announced his death on August 13 and said he was in a “happy place now.”
Article Summary: Puerto Rican boxer Prichard Colon died at 33 on August 13. Colon suffered repeated punches to the back of his head during his bout with Terrel Williams in Virginia. He later underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain and spent 221 days in a coma. After waking, he remained severely disabled and needed constant care.

Article Title: Report: Aaron Rodgers caught secretly funding police cameras that spy on his own neighbours
Article Text:
All about Aaron Rodgers' wife.(Image via Getty Images)

Aaron Rodgers says he hates being watched, turns out he secretly funded a camera network to watch his neighbors

The guy who hates being watched, watching everyone else

The other side: Is this actually that deep?

Why the cameras themselves are the real controversy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aaron Rodgers has spent years ranting about society's "sick" obsession with knowing his business. Turns out while he was busy protecting his own privacy, he was quietly bankrolling a surveillance system to keep tabs on everyone else's. A new report claims Rodgers secretly donated tens of thousands of dollars toward police license-plate cameras in his old New Jersey neighborhood, and used a shell company to hide that it was him. The irony has not been lost on anyone, least of all the internet.According to a report from the newsletter FOIAball, Rodgers dropped around $37,000 in 2024, back when he was still a Jet, on automatic license plate reader cameras for the Cedar Grove Police Department, near the mansion he was living in at the time.The donation was made through an LLC, allegedly so nobody in town would connect the dots back to him. At a city council meeting, the town manager thanked the mystery donor without naming names, calling it a "very generous donation" that gave police a useful new tool. Nobody in Cedar Grove had any idea their new surveillance upgrade came with a Hall of Fame quarterback attached, until now.This is a man who has said, on multiple occasions and on national television, that he can't stand people knowing anything about his life.He's called it a "sick society" obsessed with "entitlement to information."He's said his private life is going to stay private, full stop. And yet, behind the scenes, he was funding a system that tracks license plates of literally everyone who drives through his old neighborhood, all while making sure his own name stayed off the paperwork.To be fair to Rodgers, his paranoia isn't coming from nowhere. He's previously claimed paparazzi were flying drones over his New Jersey house, and he's talked openly about needing full-time security after Joe Burrow 's Ohio home got burglarized while Burrow was mid-game on Monday Night Football, an incident that also hit close to home given a similar break-in happened to Travis Kelce Rodgers even publicly urged other NFL players to use the league's security resources to protect their homes. So on some level, the guy funding cameras near his own house isn't shocking. What's shocking is that the cameras aren't pointed at his house, they're pointed at everyone else's, and he made sure his name wasn't attached.Not everyone's treating this as some grand hypocrisy. From LSU's side of the aisle- er, wrong story, but the same logic applies here - you could argue Rodgers did something genuinely public-minded: he paid for police equipment out of his own pocket, and the town got a free upgrade to its law enforcement toolkit.The town manager who thanked the anonymous donor didn't seem to have any complaints. If a rich guy wants to quietly pay for cop cameras instead of, say, another car, that's arguably more selfless than most celebrity spending. The read here really depends on how you feel about license plate readers in general.That's the bigger issue critics are raising, separate from Rodgers entirely: license plate readers are a lightning rod nationwide right now.Multiple towns have canceled or walked back their Flock-style camera contracts, the ACLU is running an active campaign against the company, and in some places, fed-up residents have gone as far as disguising themselves to destroy the cameras outright.The core complaint is that these systems track ordinary people's movements like where they go, when, how often, without consent or even awareness.One privacy policy expert framed the Rodgers situation as part of a bigger pattern of unelected, wealthy individuals essentially deciding how much surveillance an entire town has to live under, just because they can afford to write the check.Under that lens, it doesn't really matter whether Rodgers meant well, the point is that one person's money shouldn't get to set the privacy terms for everyone else in town.Rodgers hasn't addressed the report yet. Given how he's reacted to far smaller invasions of his own privacy, don't expect silence to last.
Article Summary: A new report claims Rodgers secretly donated tens of thousands of dollars toward police license-plate cameras in his old New Jersey neighborhood. The donation was made through an LLC, allegedly so nobody in town would connect the dots back to him. The town manager thanked the mystery donor without naming names, calling it a "very generous donation"

Article Title: Sri Lankan coach dies after altercation with cricketer in Colombo

Veteran Sri Lankan cricket coach and former school mentor Sumith Fernando has died following an altercation involving young players at a cricket facility in Colombo. Fernando, 62, passed away on Tuesday while undergoing treatment at a hospital after sustaining injuries during the incident on August 8. The coach remembered for mentoring several young cricketers, including current Sri Lanka ODI captain Kusal Mendis during his school days.According to PTI, the incident began when a group of young cricketers training at a sports facility went to get drinking water but found that there was no running water available. A disagreement reportedly broke out between the players and stadium staff over the issue. Fernando, who was present at the venue and had also worked as a curator at the Bloomfield Cricket & Athletic Club, intervened as the situation escalated.Police said a physical confrontation subsequently took place involving two players. A 17-year-old school cricketer was allegedly involved in the altercation, during which Fernando sustained injuries. He was rushed to Colombo National Hospital for treatment but died on Tuesday while receiving medical care.Police arrested the 17-year-old player on Monday on suspicion of assaulting Fernando. Since the accused is a minor, he was placed under child probation custody after being produced before a Colombo court on Tuesday.His custody has reportedly been extended until August 17 as the investigation continues.Fernando was a former coach at Prince of Wales College in Moratuwa and played a significant role in the development of several school-level cricketers. Among those he coached was Mendis, who went on to become Sri Lanka's ODI captain. Fernando later served as a grounds curator at Bloomfield Cricket & Athletic Club, a prominent club in Sri Lanka's domestic cricket structure.Fernando's funeral was held on Thursday.

Fatherhood has encouraged him to appreciate moments that might once have seemed insignificant.“You have to enjoy the moments... Article Title: How could Maxx Crosby’s top 25 ranking change the Cowboys’ 2026 trade plans?
Article Text:
Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby was voted the No. 24 player on the NFL Top 100 for 2026. (Image via Getty)

What does Maxx Crosby's No. 24 ranking say after a turbulent offseason?

Why are the Cowboys still being linked to Maxx Crosby?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Maxx Crosby is still a Las Vegas Raider. His peers also still see him as one of the NFL's best players. Neither fact has stopped another round of trade speculation.Crosby landed at No. 24 on the NFL Top 100 for 2026, the league announced Thursday. It marks his fifth consecutive appearance on the player-voted list and his fourth straight year inside the top 25. The ranking comes five months after a proposed trade to the Baltimore Ravens collapsed and with the Dallas Cowboys once again being mentioned as a possible destination.Crosby dropped only two places from No. 22 in 2025. More importantly, his production gives players plenty of reason to keep him inside the NFL's top tier.The five-time Pro Bowler finished the 2025 season with 10 sacks despite missing Las Vegas' final two games. He also recorded 28 tackles for loss, second in the NFL behind Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. Crosby led the Raiders in sacks, tackles for loss and quarterback pressures while tying for the team lead with six pass deflections, according to Raiders.com.Those numbers came during a season in which Crosby underwent another heavy workload before having meniscus surgery.The knee became a major part of his offseason for another reason.Las Vegas agreed in March to send Crosby to Baltimore for two first-round picks, but the deal never became official. ESPN reported that the Ravens backed out after medical concerns arose during Crosby's physical. Crosby remained with the Raiders, while Baltimore eventually moved elsewhere for pass-rush help.Five months later, Crosby is back on the field in Las Vegas and back inside the NFL Top 100's top 25.Raiders defensive line coach Travis Smith pointed to the habits behind that production when discussing Crosby.“The people around him are so fortunate, including coaches, to watch the routine and the discipline he approaches every day with,” Smith said, via Raiders.com.Crosby is also the second Raiders player on the 2026 list. Tight end Brock Bowers came in at No. 60.The placement offers a useful snapshot of how players around the league view Crosby after the trade saga and knee questions. He may have slipped two spots, but they still ranked him ahead of several established stars, including T.J. Watt, Chris Jones, Aidan Hutchinson and Jalen Carter.His standing around the NFL does not appear to be the uncertain part of his situation.His long-term home might be.Dallas already tried to get involved once.ESPN reported in March that the Cowboys offered Las Vegas the No. 12 overall pick as part of their pursuit of Crosby before the Ravens emerged with their two-first-round-pick package. The Cowboys ultimately moved in another direction after failing to land the Raiders star.Now, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has revived the possibility of Dallas circling back.During an appearance on “Yahoo Sports Daily,” Florio said a Crosby trade could become realistic if Las Vegas struggles once the regular season begins.“I can see a team like the Cowboys,” Florio said. “They’ve already talked about giving up future assets to improve their defense. And there was talk that they were thinking about making a play for Maxx Crosby back in March when the Ravens did. It would not surprise me if the Cowboys contend, the Raiders don’t, Crosby gets traded to Dallas.”That is speculation, not a report that Las Vegas is currently shopping Crosby or that Dallas has made another offer.There is also an obvious reason the idea continues to surface. Crosby has already shown what his trade market could look like. Baltimore was prepared to surrender two first-round picks before the physical stopped the deal, and Dallas had its own talks with Las Vegas earlier in the offseason. ESPN's reporting from March established that there was real interest, not simply a hypothetical connection between a contender and an elite pass rusher.Crosby now enters the season healthy enough to participate in Raiders training camp, removing at least some of the uncertainty that surrounded his knee in March.Las Vegas has no reason to treat a trade as inevitable. Crosby remains its top defensive player, and his No. 24 ranking is another reminder of his value.But the offseason already proved something important. A Maxx Crosby trade went much further than rumor once.That is why every time another contender needs a pass rusher, the conversation is unlikely to stay dead for long.
Article Summary: Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby was voted the No. 24 player on the NFL Top 100 for 2026. It marks his fifth consecutive appearance on the player-voted list and his fourth straight year inside the top 25. The ranking comes five months after a proposed trade to the Baltimore Ravens collapsed.
